architecturalPlan.scaleRationale: Explicit requirements are an exceptional Mediterranean courtyard estate, a US$25m value-context ambition, pitched roofs, arcades, shaded courtyards, elegant wings, and developed indoor-outdoor living. The value label informs bespoke spatial hierarchy and material depth rather than a formula for area or cost. Assumptions: an unsurveyed warm-climate setting, arrival from the south, and principal garden views to the north. The residence is intentionally single-storey: its generous 14 m-wide living hall, four substantial enclosing wings, 80 m² courtyard, shaded arrival terrace, and rear garden lounge create estate-scale presence while retaining step-free circulation and a composed low Mediterranean silhouette.
architecturalPlan.arrivalAndCirculation: A south limestone arrival terrace reaches a recessed solid entry door under a timber-soffit canopy supported by limestone posts. The primary living hall is the circulation heart: it opens directly into the central court and connects west kitchen/dining, east private-suite wing, and north guest/gallery wing through separate courtyard-facing doors. The rear north door continues to a garden terrace and open lounge pavilion. No upper level is proposed, so all occupied rooms have step-free ground-floor access.
architecturalPlan.volumeHierarchy: Primary volume: the 14 x 6 m south living hall at [0, 0.2, -7], with a 1.0 m-rise hip roof. Secondary volumes: the 6 x 16 m west dining/kitchen wing at [-8, 0.2, 0], the matching east private wing at [8, 0.2, 0], and the 14 x 6 m north guest/gallery wing at [0, 0.2, 7]; each is lower under separate 0.75 m-rise hip roofs. Their inner edges frame a 10 x 8 m paved courtyard at [0, 0.2, 0]. A low, open elliptical garden pavilion at [0, 0.2, 16] is a deliberately subordinate destination beyond the north terrace.
architecturalPlan.relationshipsAndViews: Arrival is assumed from -Z/south. The living hall and all four wings face the protected central court; the north gallery additionally faces the assumed garden at +Z. Large fitted courtyard doors establish usable indoor-outdoor links. The rear terrace connects the north wing to the open pavilion. Deep eaves, courtyard colonnade posts, and timber screens shade selected west and south-west exposures; wind, sun path, and property boundaries remain assumptions.
architecturalPlan.roofFacadeAndMaterials: Warm ivory enclosure walls sit on a limestone floor datum, with bronze doors, timber screens, and timber soffits. The principal south hall has the tallest independent hip roof; the three lower wings have separate hip roofs so the courtyard remains open to sky. Roof eaves project 0.8 m, producing deep shadow at each courtyard edge. Facades are organized as thick solid piers with one deliberate opening per bay; rectilinear limestone colonnade posts evoke an arcade rhythm beneath the eaves. True curved arches and tile texture are not represented by the available primitives.
